Basis of a reduced-rank inflation field

Source: R/basis.R
zisar_basis.Rd

Builds the knot lattice and basis functions of the reduced-rank field \(g = B\alpha\) used by zisar(..., zero_spatial = "reduced").

Usage

zisar_basis(coords, h, r_fac = 1.5)

# S3 method for class 'zisar_basis'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

coords

Two-column matrix or data frame of unit coordinates (for example centroids), in the order of the rows of W. Use projected coordinates, in the same unit as h.

h

Spacing of the knot lattice.

r_fac

Radius of the basis functions, as a multiple of h.

x

A "zisar_basis" object.

...

Not used.

Value

An object of class "zisar_basis": a list with the basis B (\(n \times K\), sparse), the knot weights Wk (\(K \times K\), sparse), the eigenvalues of Wk (eig_re, eig_im), the knot coordinates knots, the number of knots K, the spacing h and the radius r.

Details

Knots lie on a square lattice of spacing h laid over the units, and are kept where a unit lies within h of the knot. Column \(k\) of \(B\) is the bisquare function \((1 - d^2/r^2)^2\) of the distance \(d\) from knot \(k\), zero beyond the radius \(r\) = r_fac * h, and the rows of \(B\) are normalised to sum to one, so that \(g_i\) is a weighted mean of the knot values around unit \(i\) (the fixed-rank representation of Cressie and Johannesson, 2008). The knot weights \(W_K\) are rook contiguity on the lattice, row-standardised, with isolated knots linked to their nearest knot.

The spacing sets the resolution of the field: variation at scales below h is smoothed out. Each knot value should be informed by many units (the ZISAR paper uses knots 10 km apart for English neighbourhoods, about 150 units within reach of each knot); with few units per knot the Laplace approximation degrades towards that of the unit-level field.

References

Cressie, N. and Johannesson, G. (2008). Fixed rank kriging for very large spatial data sets. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B, 70(1), 209–226. doi:10.1111/j.1467-9868.2007.00633.x

See also

zisar()

Examples

# 20 x 20 lattice of units, knots every 4 units
coords <- expand.grid(x = 1:20, y = 1:20)
b <- zisar_basis(coords, h = 4)
b
#> Reduced-rank basis: 36 knots, spacing 4, radius 6, 400 units (6.2 knots per unit)
# Each unit's field value is a weighted mean of nearby knot values
range(Matrix::rowSums(b$B))
#> [1] 1 1
